proofs.notes: Dormant installation does not activate subject_of_predicate or expose output to the app.

proofs.claim: Anon and authenticated can no longer write the four Grammar release-control tables in Production, while service_role retains access.
proofs.result: Production migration ledger 20261022161426 is present. All four tables have RLS and one read policy; anon/auth retain SELECT but have no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE; service_role retains SELECT and INSERT. Local PostgreSQL migration and role test passed.
proofs.notes: This closes public writes on four tables, not all possible control-plane tables. Public SELECT remains intentionally for compatibility.

proofs.claim: The private v1.37 producer builds a live structural sentence equivalent to the current public RPC before its Rule Execution Plane call on the R051 canonical token fixture.
proofs.result: Production JSONB equality passed after removing the public RPC Rule Execution Plane field; one clause and predicate; no plane in private output. App roles lack access; zero grants; fresh input to R059 fails closed with PILOT_GRANT_INVALID.
proofs.notes: One-fixture live structural parity only; no grant and no one-rule execution.

proofs.claim: A live request can build the v1.37 structural sentence and invoke only the admitted subject_of_predicate rule without first executing other Rule Execution Plane members.
proofs.result: Production transaction built fresh pre-plane input, executed only subject_of_predicate under service_role with one uncommitted admin grant, matched the saved R051 rule-result JSONB hash, rejected the post-revocation call and rolled back. Zero grants remain.
proofs.notes: One-fixture, transaction-only Production proof. No committed grant or application integration is claimed. Existing full-plane shadow execution is separate.

proofs.claim: An administrative grant can admit one Production service_role call, and an appended revocation immediately denies the next call; a transaction rollback leaves no grant rows.
proofs.result: postgres inserted an explicit-ID grant inside a transaction; service_role returned one matching subject_of dependency; postgres appended revocation; the next service_role call raised PILOT_GRANT_INVALID; ROLLBACK left zero grants and revocations.
proofs.notes: Transactional test, not a committed grant or activated rule.

proofs.claim: At the observed deployed versions, four inspected app analysis server functions have no pilot or canonical shadow call and the last-24-hour canonical shadow log has no successful request.
proofs.result: Deployed analyze-text v172, grammar-analysis-orchestrator v75, language-graph-engine v64 and job-orchestrator v113 lack pilot/canonical references; private SQL ACL blocks app roles; canonical shadow logs show one 401 and zero 200 in the default last-24-hour window.
proofs.notes: Bounded snapshot only; canonical shadow can return language_graph to an authorized service caller. R055 whole-app isolation remains UNVERIFIED.

proofs.claim: Legacy pilot-audit functions are executable by anon and authenticated, while the comparator output tables have RLS enabled with no policies.
proofs.result: Production ACL read shows anon/auth EXECUTE on apply/build pilot audit and volatile comparator; anon/auth INSERT grants on shadow batches/comparisons coexist with RLS and zero policies. Corpus cases table has no RLS. No role-level invocation was attempted.
proofs.notes: Do not claim successful anon/auth comparator execution or app graph leakage from grants alone. Review this surface separately before Production pilot.

proofs.claim: At the observed deployed versions, no known app analysis path invokes the new canonical Grammar Graph or private SQL pilot, and direct app SQL roles cannot execute their functions.
proofs.result: All 53 deployed Edge Function bundles were searched: only canonical shadow itself references the v1.40 structural RPC; no deployed function references the private pilot. Local app source has no canonical/pilot call; anon/auth SQL EXECUTE is denied; canonical shadow had one 401 and no 200 in the prior 24 hours.
proofs.notes: Scoped to the new Grammar Graph and known deployed/app sources. External service-key callers remain outside the inventory. The legacy language-graph-engine is separate and unchanged.

proofs.claim: The existing SQL Rule Execution Plane can safely grant one controlled subject_of_predicate pilot without exposing graph output to the app.
proofs.result: R065 proved one short-lived Production grant and revocation. R071 current-source diagnostic corpus matched 9/12 expected subject relations, missed three and produced zero edges for two nonfinite controls. The target subject rule remains inactive, release shadow and active grants zero. Broader activation still needs structural coverage and independent subject disambiguation.
proofs.notes: Separate from SUBJECT_OF_PREDICATE_ACTIVATION_READY, which tracks canonical R048M scheduler admission and structural S0 support.

proofs.claim: One short-lived committed Production grant admits exactly one private SQL subject_of_predicate execution; a separately committed revocation denies later calls.
proofs.result: Grant ID 1 was committed, service_role produced one subject_of dependency for Katten sover with exact R051 rule-result hash parity, revocation was committed, the next call raised PILOT_GRANT_INVALID, and zero active grants remain.
proofs.notes: This is one bounded pilot, not global activation or application integration. The legacy graph route was unchanged.

proofs.claim: Before R067, the SQL pipeline produced subject_of for three simple probes but stopped before predicate and clause for Hunden spiser fisken despite resolved POS and verb morphology.
proofs.result: Katten sover, Jeg sover and Han er glad each yielded one predicate, clause and subject_of edge. Hunden spiser fisken yielded zero of all three; V32 base clause count is zero although structural POS is noun-verb-noun and spiser has resolved verb morphology.
proofs.notes: Historical gap invalidated by R067 V32 migration. Four manually assembled RPC token envelopes were diagnostic, not live canonical-surface captures.

proofs.claim: The bounded V32 noun bootstrap now produces a resolved predicate, clause and subject_of edge for a three-token noun-verb-noun sentence while preserving the tested two-token and pronoun cases.
proofs.result: Migration 20261022202018 is in the Production ledger; V32 definition md5 changed from a373f16bdb95aa9e30bca3d9aa108f4f to 13447a8763b15dbfbbf1ec65df7068fe. All four positive cases yielded one subject_of edge. Three negative controls yielded zero. ACL, shadow release and global rule state stayed unchanged.
proofs.notes: Historical Production definition superseded by R069. Diagnostic seven-case corpus with manually assembled RPC inputs. Not general grammatical correctness or full activation.

proofs.claim: Current canonical source modules generate identity-preserving SQL inputs; on a selected fourteen-case read-only Production corpus, six of twelve expected subject relations are produced and six are absent, with zero edges on two nonfinite controls.
proofs.result: R051 canonical projection test passed. Fourteen current-source canonical input envelopes were sent to the Production SQL RPC. Six positives matched subject and predicate surfaces with canonical parity; six valid positives lacked predicate/clause; two nonfinite controls produced no edge. Object ambiguity and additional finite reading explain two failures; longer or reordered structure explains four.
proofs.notes: Historical 6/12 snapshot superseded by R069 8/12 after V32 migration. Selected diagnostic corpus, not a representative accuracy rate. Local source input generation is proven; deployed Edge bundle parity on all fourteen sentences is not claimed. No grant or application integration.

proofs.claim: The R069 Production V32 definition preserves the subject/predicate core for two additional ambiguous postfinite noun surfaces in the selected canonical-source corpus, without assigning their object identity or inflection.
proofs.result: Production ledger 20261023073508 and V32 md5 085d185eb036701eef8ce881a840f165 confirmed. Eight of twelve expected subject edges matched, four absent, two nonfinite controls zero. New Jenta leser boken and Barnet drikker vann edges retain canonical subject identity. Release remains shadow, global rule inactive, zero active grants.
proofs.notes: Historical 8/12 Production snapshot superseded by R071 9/12. Diagnostic corpus only. The resolved clause covers the subject/predicate core, not the postfinite token. Noun candidate existence is not a validated object relation, sense, gender or inflection. Deployed Edge parity on all inputs remains open.

proofs.claim: The graph distinguishes a subject-initial noun-verb-noun clause from a valid object-initial clause using independent syntax evidence before assigning subject_of.
proofs.result: Open. R079 read-only Production pairs show V32 resolves Fisken spiser hunden from initial noun position, while Meg ser han remains without a clause. No independent noun subject authority or runtime pronoun-case feature was observed.
proofs.notes: Do not infer a specific wrong edge from the current five control probes; this is an unproven generalization risk.

proofs.claim: The current Production token resolver retains two noun bok homographs and a third unknown-POS exact-base boken candidate, while morphology returns no reading for boken.
proofs.result: Surface resolution ambiguous_unresolved with three candidates. The two source-backed bok noun candidates have distinct lexeme and dictionary article IDs 6790/106786; both source forms tag boken singular definite, accept en/ei and list boka as alternative. Third boken candidate has unknown POS and no verification status. Morphology is no_morph_reading with zero readings.
proofs.notes: Source form candidates support noun/POS and form hypotheses, but do not prove native graph recognition, generation, explanation or selected homograph. The realized boken form is masculine definite singular; feminine counterpart is boka.

proofs.claim: The graph itself can analyze, validate, explain and generate bok I/II definite singular forms with provenance while retaining unresolved homograph and gender alternatives.
proofs.result: Open. For boken, canonical morphology reports no_morph_reading and zero readings; dictionary form lookup alone is insufficient as graph-rule execution proof.
proofs.notes: This gap is separate from the bounded SQL subject_of_predicate pilot. Stored paradigms may be comparison evidence but must not silently become the graph's answer authority.

proofs.claim: The R071 Production V32 definition preserves the subject/predicate core for a bounded three-token noun + finite verb + adjective-neuter surface without asserting an adverbial analysis of the tail.
proofs.result: Production ledger 20261023080811 and V32 md5 28301d551fa68a9cfe356d75ec35149f confirmed. Selected canonical-source corpus matched 9/12 expected subject edges, missed three and produced zero on two nonfinite controls. Jenta leser raskt produced one subject_of; Hunden spiser stor produced none. Target rule remains inactive, release shadow, active pilot grants zero.
proofs.notes: Diagnostic corpus only. The adjective-neuter source form licenses a syntax-core path; it is not an adverb morphology reading or proof of tail correctness. Three longer/reordered structural cases and SVO/OVS ambiguity remain. Nine other grammar_rules rows were active at observation; the target subject rule was inactive.

proofs.claim: On current Production and canonical-source input, Hunden spiser fisken i dag stops before predicate/clause; the i dag tail has no resolved MWE or attachment in this execution.
proofs.result: V32 clause, predicate, resolved clause and subject_of counts are zero. Hunden and fisken each have a noun candidate; spiser has a finite verb reading. i has no lexical candidate, dag is noun/adverb ambiguous. Multiword expression and clause attachment resolved counts are zero; phrase builder has NP:1, VP:2, NP:3 and a hypothesis NP:5.
proofs.notes: This proves a bounded observed gap, not that a temporal-tail producer is absent from all code or data.

proofs.claim: The graph can preserve a verified subject/predicate core across an unresolved or resolved temporal tail without asserting correctness for the whole sentence or silently discarding the tail.
proofs.result: Open. The present five-token execution yields no core; R073 found that a verified i dag expression is not projected to runtime MWE facts and the MWE builder runs after V32. A length-only V32 relaxation would not prove tail syntax.
proofs.notes: Keep tail status separate from clause-core status and do not select a lexical reading for dag from dictionary candidates alone.

proofs.claim: The verified i dag expression exists in the lexicon but has no runtime MWE fact, while the current RPC executes V32 before the MWE builder and the v1.37 PP rule is not enabled.
proofs.result: The i dag lexeme is an active multi-source verified expression. Runtime multiword facts have no [i,dag] entry in any release, and the current sentence has zero candidate and matched MWE occurrences. i is rejected only by a learning-dictionary admission rule; no grammar lexical class member for i exists. In the current RPC V32 precedes the MWE builder; compiled PP rule is absent from v1.37 membership.
proofs.notes: Do not treat dictionary exclusion as evidence that i is ungrammatical. A lexical expression entry is not executable MWE evidence. Adding a late MWE fact alone cannot repair an earlier V32 zero-clause result.

proofs.claim: A source-backed i dag occurrence can be resolved with canonical span identity before clause-core admission, or trigger a controlled re-evaluation, without asserting arbitrary i + noun expressions as temporal adverbs.
proofs.result: Open. The source entry exists, but the runtime has no corresponding MWE fact and currently runs MWE recognition after V32.
proofs.notes: Do not mutate immutable v1.37 release membership or classify a generic preposition phrase as the lexical adverb i dag merely from adjacent surfaces. Preserve candidate versus resolved status and source provenance.

proofs.claim: The current Production RPC emits a source-backed candidate for the exact i dag span before V32, preserving canonical token IDs, without granting a resolved syntactic function.
proofs.result: Positive exact span one candidate; reversed dag i and i boken zero candidates. Resolved function, V32 clause and subject edge remain zero for the five-token case. Full diagnostic corpus unchanged at 9/12 positive subject edges and zero on two nonfinite controls. Production ledger 20261023082759; RPC md5 81ae1453781a9ee00e67863086ec4bb9.
proofs.notes: Candidate only; does not prove a temporal adjunct, clause-core survival, subject relation, rule activation, or that v1.49/v1.50 current implementations are complete.

proofs.claim: Inspected historical v1.48/v1.49/v1.50 boundaries do not demonstrate an existing runtime fix for the observed i dag clause-core gap.
proofs.result: v1.48 concerns TAM and has canonical TAM source modules. v1.49 historical status is complex/non-local source-data-blocked. v1.50 punctuation closure records surface projection PASS but grammar source payload absent, runtime wiring NO and activation NO. v1.50 surface evidence may be reused for the question-order case.
proofs.notes: Historical archive conclusions are architectural evidence, not a current Production behavior proof. The claim is limited to inspected sources and artifacts.

proofs.claim: In the inspected current Production SQL and tracked canonical adapter, the R074 early source expression candidate has no downstream semantic or graph consumer.
proofs.result: Production public pg_proc definitions reference the early field only in its producer and parent RPC. The checked MWE, clause, attachment and rule-plane functions do not reference it. The tracked legacy MWE adapter reads the separate late multiword layer. R074 remains candidate-only with no clause or subject edge for the long-tail case.
proofs.notes: The absence claim is limited to inspected public SQL definitions and tracked adapter source; it does not exclude external or dynamic consumers.

proofs.claim: A source-backed i dag candidate is mapped to a runtime occurrence that can be independently resolved and used for clause-core survival while retaining canonical span and avoiding false resolution of i boken or dag i.
proofs.result: Open. R075 found no consumer for the existing early candidate; no resolved adjunct or clause-core survival has been demonstrated.
proofs.notes: Do not promote a lexical expression to a syntactic adverb merely because its surfaces match. Do not change immutable v1.37 membership.

proofs.claim: The existing V32 can recover a bounded subject/predicate core from the first three tokens of a five-token input, but this recovery alone cannot distinguish i dag from near-negative tails or validate the whole sentence.
proofs.result: For Hunden spiser fisken followed by i dag, i boken, or dag i, the full five-token run has zero clauses while an in-query V32 rerun over the first three existing structural tokens yields one core clause. Only i dag yields an early source expression candidate. No Production mutation occurred.
proofs.notes: This is diagnostic core recoverability, not a resolved adjunct, sentence parse, subject-rule activation or proof that the two near-negative sentences are ungrammatical.

proofs.claim: An isolated scoped-core projection can retain canonical identities and deferred tokens while treating the V32 prefix clause as a candidate and emitting no graph edge.
proofs.result: A read-only Production fixture with six inputs passed 57 executable checks. The long-tail input retains one separate source expression candidate and three deferred tokens. Two near-negative tails retain no expression candidate. Fisken spiser hunden remains a candidate despite a V32 clause. The question-order and nonfinite controls produce no candidate. No graph edge is emitted.
proofs.notes: This proves a test-only representation and invariants, not a Production producer, syntactic truth, graph transition or activated rule.

proofs.claim: The scoped-core candidate is produced and consumed by the live grammar runtime without losing token identity, silently resolving a tail, or emitting an unauthorized subject edge.
proofs.result: Open. R077 only exercised a standalone projection over saved Production data.
proofs.notes: Do not promote the SVO/OVS-sensitive noun-verb-noun subject to resolved solely because V32 returns a clause.

proofs.claim: An isolated candidate-only span patch for R077 is accepted by the existing canonical graph transition without grammar edges, while the legacy clause adapter would emit a candidate subject_of edge from the same hypothesis.
proofs.result: Deno test and type check passed. Fifty-seven checks across six source-backed inputs: canonical surface IDs match, graph invariants pass, candidate nodes retain status and evidence/provenance, graph patch is idempotent, and no grammar edge appears. A control invocation of clausePatchFromLegacyV11 on a candidate hypothesis emitted a candidate subject_of edge.
proofs.notes: Test-only graph patch. No Production runtime wiring, deployed Edge code, rule admission, or activation was changed. Candidate nodes do not establish subject identity.

proofs.claim: Current Production exposes a subject_pronoun lexical signal but no observed case feature or independent noun role decision in the tested V32-to-clause-to-subject_of path.
proofs.result: Read-only minimal pairs: Han ser meg resolves subject token 1; Meg ser han produces no clause; Fisken spiser hunden resolves subject token 1 by positional V32 bootstrap. meg is tagged pronoun but has no morphology reading/case feature. Existing pronoun.general.classification.personal_case_inflection is source_verified yet not compiled into grammar_rules. This proves the bounded runtime observation, not general absence of other possible authorities.
proofs.notes: han can also be an object form; subject_pronoun class membership alone does not prove syntactic role. No Production write, deployment, or rule activation in this audit.

proofs.claim: Production has a source-verified Bokmal personal-pronoun case paradigm designated for grammar runtime, but no linked grammar_rule_sources or compiled grammar_rules row for it.
proofs.result: The specific pronoun.personal.forms.bokmal.paradigm candidate (section 4.1.1) lists jeg/meg, du/deg, han/ham, hun/henne, den/den, det/det, vi/oss, dere/dere, de/dem and is marked KEEP_GRAMMAR_RUNTIME. Production has zero grammar_rules rows for its code and zero grammar_rule_sources links for its candidate ID. The broader personal_case_inflection candidate is KEEP_REFERENCE_ONLY.
proofs.notes: This is the specific source authority for the case-form mapping. It does not by itself prove runtime morphology, subject-role resolution, or rule activation.

proofs.claim: A four-sentence slice of the manually annotated UD Norwegian Bokmaal test set can be aligned with current Production RPC inputs and reveals separate OVS role and lexical coverage gaps.
proofs.result: The two gold OVS examples Det har hun and Det har jeg have PRON/VERB/PRON readings in Production but no case feature or resolved clause. Two gold SVO noun examples also have no clause, with one or more lexical candidates missing. All four examples were read-only Production RPC calls. This selected slice is diagnostic, not an accuracy estimate.
proofs.notes: UD Norwegian Bokmaal test corpus is CC BY-SA 4.0. Alignment excludes punctuation in the three-token SQL structural RPC input and compares content-token roles only. No Production mutation or rule activation.

proofs.claim: The source-backed Bokmal pronoun paradigm is runtime eligible but currently lacks an operator mapping, validated manifest, materialized rule and canonical integration.
proofs.result: Production assess_candidate_operator_capability_v1 returned operator_mapping_missing with zero mappings for execution role morphological_paradigm. assess_candidate_activation_readiness_v2 returned needs_manifest, activation_ready=false, and zero materialized, validated-manifest, operator-ready and canonical-integrated rules. The bounded SQL subject_of_predicate grant was already executed and revoked in R065; current active grants remain zero.
proofs.notes: Read-only preflight. Runtime eligible is not activation ready. No Production mutation or new pilot grant.

proofs.claim: On a second source-backed input, Jeg sover, the existing subject_of_predicate executor produces one canonical token-to-predicate dependency with exact parity to its full shadow release result.
proofs.result: The private pre-rule-plane builder yielded resolved clause and predicate, subject token index 1 and canonical token ID tok:0:0:3. Direct execute_dependency_pattern_rule_v2 produced one Jeg-to-sover subject_of dependency with supported actions, materialized trace and canonical parity. Its JSONB equaled the subject rule result in the full shadow release; both md5 values were 2ae8aacc33495e4237a4baaaf7ea42c7. Active grants remained zero.
proofs.notes: Direct read-only executor call on one additional input. No admission grant, persistent write, app delivery or global activation. R065 separately proved admitted execution on Katten sover. This does not prove general subject disambiguation.

proofs.claim: A source-backed isolated operator contract can generate and recognize Bokmal personal-pronoun case forms in both directions while retaining ambiguous identical forms and candidate provenance.
proofs.result: Forty-two checks passed over nine source pairs and eleven generation-recognition paths. meg resolves as candidate Acc form of jeg; den and det retain Nom and Acc candidates; unknown words, unsupported case, unverified source, wrong execution role and malformed source are rejected. Outputs retain source candidate ID and section.
proofs.notes: Isolated tool only. No operator approval, manifest, materialized grammar rule, canonical token producer, Production mutation or activation. Case candidates do not themselves assign subject/object role.

proofs.claim: An isolated source-backed pronoun case producer can add nonexhaustive candidate lexical and morph readings to the canonical graph without changing token identity or creating subject/object edges.
proofs.result: Deno execution and type check passed. Twenty-six checks across Meg ser han, Jeg ser meg and Den ser det confirm graph invariants, stable token IDs, idempotence, candidate-only readings, nonexhaustive case evidence, source provenance and no subject/object edges.
proofs.notes: Test-only graph patch. No Production runtime wiring, approved operator, manifest, materialized rule, grant, activation or app output. The source statement does not establish objective han as impossible; absence of a reading cannot reject it.

proofs.claim: A source-backed morphological_paradigm producer feeds case candidates into the service-only SQL pilot before predicate/clause building, allowing the existing subject rule to distinguish a bounded SVO/OVS pair while retaining ambiguous controls.
proofs.result: Production migration applied. The private pilot built resolved clauses and one direct subject_of edge for Jeg ser meg (subject 1) and Meg ser han (subject 3). Det har jeg and Den ser det remained unresolved with no subject_of edge; Katten sover retained subject 1. Local manifest/operator contract passed 45 checks. The manifest is draft, template blocked, paradigm materialized rules zero, active grants zero, and public RPC hash unchanged.
proofs.notes: Bounded service-only pilot proof. Case candidates are nonexhaustive; the SQL clause is provisional under shadow. No public RPC wiring, validated manifest, global activation, admission grant or app output.

proofs.claim: The service-only pilot now keeps the source-backed pronoun case contrast as a soft subject candidate, without resolving an OVS clause or executing subject_of solely from case.
proofs.result: Production correction applied. Meg ser han now has proposed subject token 3 with paradigm and separate case_selection provenance, zero resolved clauses and zero subject_of edges. Existing SVO controls still execute, ambiguous same-form cases and coordination remain unresolved. Fisken spiser hunden still resolves positionally through pre-existing V32 and remains an open defect.
proofs.notes: Corrective migration supersedes R086's hard subject resolution. The candidate's source says hovedregelen, with known exceptions. No validated case_selection manifest, grant or global activation.

policy.automatic_transition: effective PROVEN->STALE only; never auto-promote declared proof status
